result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.single_target_shortest_path()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find a shortest path from every node to a target. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L46560-L46641){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.single_target_shortest_path( target, cutoff=None, weighted=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Single-target shortest paths](/assets/graphs/single-target-shortest-path.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A one-way street network: shop to home, home to park, park to station. With the target station (outlined), every node that can reach it gets the shortest path from itself to the station, following the arrows (accent color): shop goes through home and park, home through park, park directly, and station maps to itself." width="100%"} The mirror image of `single_source_shortest_path()`: for every node that can reach `target`, one shortest path from that node *to* the target (following edge direction). Use it to route everything toward a sink, such as all traffic toward an exit, all requests toward a server, or every state toward a goal state. On an undirected graph it gives the source paths reversed. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The destination node, as an ID or label. [cutoff]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional maximum distance; nodes farther away are left out. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag. Negative weights are allowed on directed graphs (Bellman-Ford). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : For every node that reaches `target`, a path as node IDs ending at `target` (the target maps to `[target]`). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the target does not exist or a negative cycle can reach it. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} One search over reversed edges from the target (breadth-first, Dijkstra or Bellman-Ford, as in `predecessor()`); each path follows the first recorded next hop. Matches the lengths of NetworkX's `single_target_shortest_path`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a one-way street network, which routes lead to the station? ::: {#4c511c4a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec streets = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["home", "park", "shop", "station"]) streets.add_edges([("home", "park"), ("park", "station"), ("shop", "home")]) paths = streets.single_target_shortest_path("station") {streets.get_label_from_id(n): [streets.get_label_from_id(x) for x in p] for n, p in paths.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'home': ['home', 'park', 'station'], 'park': ['park', 'station'], 'shop': ['shop', 'home', 'park', 'station'], 'station': ['station']} ``` ::: :::
